items.title: August Lanoix Interview, 1961-04-19
items.q: Harrison Bradley. Yeah, Harrison Bradley. He was a baritone and trombone player. So he was very good. I don't know if he's dead or on the left. Is he dead? I think he is.

ctx.x: And they had some alto and baritone players in those days. Do you remember who some of them were?

One was, I don't remember the alto, I don't remember one alto player, he just died. Paul Barberin's father and Cisador Barberin. He was one and Adolf Alexander, I don't know if you remember. I know his son, no. His daddy, I mean the dad. Well he played a good baritone too, the son. And what he had several other guys, but I mean, yeah, there's one fella, he's, I think he must be there too, Georgia Hooker. He was from Alexandria. He was formerly a trumpet player. He was a good baritone player. Now they had one…
I think so, yeah, I'm sure he does. Harrison Barnes, who died last year, used to play trombone. And I know he played with Hooker, he told us about him. I guess he played baritone horn some too.
